title: Finite and compatible completed local bases of the root tower
statement:
For any scheme on which l is invertible, the concrete finite root modules [def-pur-twist-sheaves] admit etale unit trivializations and have finite geometric stalks. The completed root module admits a pro-etale unit trivialization, and its ordinary finite scalar reductions are the prescribed finite root modules. There is no coefficient field or derived-completeness assertion.

theorem purTwistRootLocalModels (S : Scheme.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    [∀ x : S, Invertible (l : S.residueField x)] :
    (∀ n : ℕ,
      (∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → S.ProEt)
        (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ ProEt.mk (𝟙 S)),
        Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ (ProEt.precoverage S).coverings _ ∧
        (∀ i : I, Etale (U i).hom) ∧
        ∀ i : I, Nonempty ((purTwistRootsModule S l n).over (U i) ≅
          (SheafOfModules.unit (purTwistRing S (purTwistFiniteRing S l n))).over (U i))) ∧
      (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S),
        Finite ((proEtaleGeometricStalk (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) s
          (proEtaleRootsOfUnitySheaf S (l ^ (n + 1)))) : Type (u + 1)))) ∧
    ((∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → S.ProEt)
        (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ ProEt.mk (𝟙 S)),
        Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ (ProEt.precoverage S).coverings _ ∧
        ∀ i : I, Nonempty ((purTwistZlModule S l).over (U i) ≅
          (SheafOfModules.unit (purTwistRing S (purTwistZlCompletion S l))).over (U i))) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty
        (SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsOfUniverses.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1}
          (purTwistZlProjection S l n)
          (purTwistZlModule S l) ≅ purTwistRootsModule S l n))

proof.text: The residue-field invertibility assumption makes ell a unit in global sections, by the local-ring residue criterion and the unit-germ criterion. Pull the universal primitive-root scheme for ell^(n+1) back along S -> Spec Gamma(S,O). It is etale and surjective. Its universal root has unit differences between distinct powers. The proved constantRootsIso identifies the constant cyclic abelian sheaf with the source root sheaf on each covering member. Identify the latter with the concrete kernel sheaf via its canonical sections equivalence. Localization restriction and the slice-site equivalence transport this isomorphism to the required slice. Every additive map between these finite cyclic module sheaves is linear: locally lift a scalar to the constant Z/ell^(n+1) presheaf, represent it by an integer, and use preservation of integer scalar multiplication. For a geometric stalk, lift the corresponding site point through the covering. Its fiber on that slice is the original stalk, and the constant finite-group fiber is finite. The constructions include empty covering members and the empty base.

Apply the proved compatible primitive-root diagram basis theorem, using the global unit just obtained. Compare the concrete positive-index root tower with the source sheafified root tower shifted by one. The concrete transition followed by its kernel inclusion is the ell-th power, so the canonical sections equivalences form a diagram isomorphism. Constant sheafification commutes with forgetting the ring structure; this similarly identifies the underlying additive coefficient tower with the shifted constant residue tower. Weakly-etale inverse image is localization restriction. The dense slice equivalence therefore transports the given diagram isomorphism to the slices of one pro-etale cover.

Take limits of the slice diagram isomorphisms. Restriction and forgetting rings preserve these limits. The resulting additive limit isomorphism commutes with every finite projection. Its component maps are linear by the finite cyclic argument of step 1. Joint injectivity of the coefficient limit projections and the coordinate specification of purTwistZlAction then prove linearity of the limit isomorphism. Form the global scalar-extension map induced by the actual root-limit projection. On a covering slice, extend the completed unit basis along the coefficient projection; the extendedBasisIso construction identifies its source with the finite coefficient unit. The projection formula shows on each pure tensor that the global map is this extended basis followed by the inverse finite basis. It is therefore locally an isomorphism, hence globally an isomorphism by the coversTop criterion. This needs no separate coefficient-completion quotient theorem.
